items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Get Stanley Cowell on the piano and Benny Maupin on the saxophone... That was my first record date... That had Benny Maupin on bass clarinet, tenor, voice... It was great to play with Gary and Benny.

ctx.x: Monk, yeah. So when he had his label I talked to him about doing my own record and he said to me, “Well, think about what you want to do and you get it together. Come to me and do it.” I’ll say one of my mentors who I really had a lot of fun with when I came to New York and was really great was Roy Haynes. So Roy Haynes and I used to hang out. Still stay in touch with each other a lot. I used to call him “Papa Daddy.” So I wrote this piece for him. I played the melodica so I decided I’d like to do a melodica/drum…
We’re going to run out of tape here quickly but I just wanted to ask. So when you did the recording with Miles in November of 68’ were you officially a member of the band at that point?

items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: Bitches Brew was basically kind of a jam session with ... Bennie Maupin would play, different players would solo on top of that.

ctx.x: And there’s a quote in here from you, “I got around so well on Miles’ music because I like the unexpected.” Was “Bitches Brew” an unexpected situation for you or had you been sort of set up for that?

Yeah I was set up and prepared. I’m from Chicago, where I played various kinds of music. So I didn’t have any biases toward all the so-called genres of music. You know “Bitches Brew” was basically kind of a jam session with — not highly arranged, but with, you know, melodic interludes in between things. And then Miles let the tapes roll and got a groove that he liked and then he would play or somebody — Bennie Maupin would play, different players would solo on top of that. And then through Teo Macero, © Fillius…
his producer, through his artistry of putting all the different tracks together to tell a story, he did that very well.
